title: Children's Bedtime Stories — Episodic (Ages 3–4)
summary: Original sequential, single-narrator bedtime adventures for ages 3–4, primarily age three. Season one explores Willow Bend and completes the Little-Light Walk; season two travels west to Far Meadow, meets Wendy, and completes a ribbon picnic. Season three travels east past Round Pond into Reed Meadow, meets Todd and Aunt Pat, and finishes Ben’s Book of Little Sounds. Places, relationships and objects persist between episodes; every night closes gently. Non-spoken caregiver explanations and citations do not assert developmental or sleep effects. Season four revisits the southern orchard, corrects one bend on Amy’s real map, and grows an explicitly imaginary Button Town game around the two-trunk Doorway Tree; its pretend map ends safely at the Story House. Season five stays near Story House, where a small garden is permitted, seeded, observed over several visits and celebrated as a little patch of seedlings; it does not grow instant flowers or reset other objects. Season six crosses several evenings from a thin waxing crescent to a full Moon, following distinct observations and silly games at established homes; the same valley, friendships, garden, maps and shelves persist. Season seven introduces Sue and Grandpa Ed at a small stone cottage near the fenced old mill; the six existing friends build relationships in separate playful visits, and Sue chooses the round-window symbol for Amy's real yellow map. No established geography or Story House collection is reset. Season eight changes the familiar Story House doorway: Grandpa Ed repairs its stiff hinge, the old squeak disappears, new quiet and comic greetings follow, and Amy records the new click beside the old squeak mark on her map. Season nine expands the known world west beyond Far Meadow via a green bus to Market Street in a neighboring town; individual visits to a bakery, library, clock and square end with a fold-out extension of Amy’s physical map and a returned library book. Season ten returns after further weeks to the original Story House garden: the spring radishes have been harvested, sunflowers have grown tall and one opens, the original garden sign moves to remain readable, and a new picture and flower dot record the change without erasing earlier growth. Season eleven brings Ben's original six-page Book of Little Sounds from the Story House on the green bus to Market Street library for a small Sunday storytelling table and returns it home unchanged except for a loose library thank-you bookmark.
assumed_background: Age 3–4; prior episodes enrich continuity but each episode includes enough context to enjoy on its own.
series_title: Willow Bend and the Little Lights

lectures.title: Amy and the Map with Room for More
lectures.description: Amy begins a yellow map of Willow Bend and learns how many small places can fit into one familiar day.

lectures.title: Ben and the Humming Bridge
lectures.description: Ben listens to different footsteps and reeds on Pebble Bridge, while a violet pouch hints at someone farther along the path.

lectures.title: A Small Hello at Round Pond
lectures.description: Amy and Ben meet Kim, a careful observer of ripples, and find that friendship can begin with a quiet shared moment.

lectures.title: The Apple That Went Traveling
lectures.description: An especially round apple takes a rolling trip through the orchard and turns into a shared joke and a new mark on the map.

lectures.title: The Lantern That Leaned
lectures.description: Ben experiments with an orange paper lantern that leans to one side and discovers its tilt can become part of its charm.

lectures.title: The Little-Light Walk
lectures.description: The friends follow their mapped path through Willow Bend, recall the places they know, and watch the valley lights together.

lectures.title: The Other Side of Bell Hill
lectures.description: Amy, Ben, and Kim cross Bell Hill with Grandma May, discover Far Meadow, and meet Wendy, whose blue-ribboned hat likes the wind.

lectures.title: Ben's Very Big Pocket
lectures.description: Ben stuffs a coat pocket with ordinary treasures and opens a very silly temporary museum on Far Meadow's Sitting Stone.

lectures.title: Kim and the Soft-Grass Path
lectures.description: Wendy shows the friends a sheltered clover nook behind the Windbreak Tree; Kim helps choose how the newly discovered place appears on the map.

lectures.title: The Shadow with a Very Long Scarf
lectures.description: Wendy visits Willow Bend, sees the Story House and lantern, and the friends notice their shadows looking different as the day passes.

lectures.title: The Ribbon That Wouldn't Sit Still
lectures.description: Friends gather in the Story House to arrange an orange, blue, and violet banner while the breeze gives their decorations ideas of its own.

lectures.title: The Picnic Beyond the Hill
lectures.description: The friends share a breezy picnic beneath the Windbreak Tree and recognize the places and friendships that now belong on Amy's expanding map.

lectures.title: The Path Past Round Pond
lectures.description: Kim leads the friends east of Round Pond to Reed Meadow, and Ben starts a blue notebook of little sounds.

lectures.title: Ben's Very Serious Listening Hat
lectures.description: Ben makes a paper listening hat, discovers that it mostly crinkles, and fills a second notebook page with bridge sounds.

lectures.title: The Croak Behind the Grass
lectures.description: A rounded bup leads the friends to Todd, a young frog in yellow boots, and a new friendship begins at Reed Meadow.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Two Kinds of Wind
lectures.description: Wendy travels east with Aunt Kay, meets Todd, and helps fill the sound book with the different rustles of two meadows.

lectures.title: The Plink Under the Eaves
lectures.description: From a dry Story House, the friends trace a rainy plink to drops hitting a watering can and add its picture to their book.

lectures.title: The Last Little Sound
lectures.description: Friends from both sides of the valley read Ben’s five pages at Story House, discover a final paper sound, and shelve the completed book.

lectures.title: Amy and the Bent Orchard Path
lectures.description: Amy visits the orchard, discovers that her straight map line misses a path bend, and names the two-trunk Doorway Tree.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Doorway Tree
lectures.description: Wendy visits the orchard for the first time, and the children invent Button Town through the ordinary two-trunk Doorway Tree.

lectures.title: Ben's Very Important Tiny Post Office
lectures.description: Ben opens a pretend post office at the Doorway Tree with drawings, slipper wheels and a basket that keeps all the real letters.

lectures.title: Todd and the Lake the Size of a Teacup
lectures.description: On Todd’s first orchard visit, an ordinary puddle becomes Lake Teacup in the friends’ imagined Button Town.

lectures.title: Kim and Button Town's Quietest Place
lectures.description: The children add a bell, invisible socks and a bell-free resting spot to Button Town without asking everyone to play the same way.

lectures.title: A Map for Two Kinds of Places
lectures.description: All five friends make a separate imaginary map of Button Town and place it beside the completed Book of Little Sounds.

lectures.title: The Small Patch Behind the Story House
lectures.description: Amy discovers a small sunny patch behind Story House; Grandma May asks permission to use it as a garden, and Amy adds its location to her real map.

lectures.title: Ben's Sign for the Seeds
lectures.description: Ben creates a sign far too large for their small garden, while Grandma May helps the children plant radish and sunflower seeds with sensible row labels.

lectures.title: Kim and the Day Nothing Happened
lectures.description: Kim checks the garden on several successive days without seeing sprouts, but notices rain, an insect, differences in soil moisture and a place to stand.

lectures.title: Todd and the Little Green Hook
lectures.description: Todd visits from Reed Meadow, sees the first three tiny radish seedlings, and draws them as green hooks and hats.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Hat for a Sunflower
lectures.description: Wendy visits the garden after the radish sprouts open their first leaves and a sunflower shoot appears; the children make pretend hats for the sign rather than placing paper on the plant.

lectures.title: The Little Growing Garden
lectures.description: All five friends revisit the garden, notice two sunflower shoots and a still-bare space, draw a picture of the little garden as it exists now, and store it at Story House.

lectures.title: Amy and the Silver Smile
lectures.description: After checking the real Story House garden, Amy notices a thin waxing crescent Moon above Blue Door Cottage and imagines it as a silver smile.

lectures.title: Ben's Moon Hat Department
lectures.description: Ben opens a make-believe hat shop for the Moon, a basket, and a pencil; later he observes that the waxing crescent looks broader than Amy described several nights before.

lectures.title: Kim's Moon in the Pond
lectures.description: Kim watches the half-lit first-quarter Moon reflected in Round Pond; ripples scramble the reflection, but not the Moon in the sky.

lectures.title: Wendy's Nearly Round Biscuit
lectures.description: Wendy and Aunt Kay make funny Moon-shaped biscuits in Far Meadow while a waxing gibbous Moon appears over the Windbreak Tree.

lectures.title: Todd and the Moon Behind the Reeds
lectures.description: From the safe dry path at Reed Meadow, Todd finds that stepping beside a nearby reed can hide or reveal an almost-full Moon.

lectures.title: Five Windows and One Moon
lectures.description: The five friends share funny Moon observations at Story House; as the full Moon rises at sunset, each returns to a familiar home with a grown-up.

lectures.title: The Blue Cart on the Orchard Path
lectures.description: Amy and Grandma May meet Sue and Grandpa Ed as they move into the stone cottage with a round window by the orchard path.

lectures.title: Ben and the Castle Bakery
lectures.description: Ben and Sue turn empty moving boxes into a castle bakery, but Sue keeps her favorite cushion for sitting instead of using it as a roof.

lectures.title: Kim and the Little Round Window
lectures.description: Kim visits Sue to admire the round window; three familiar pebbles become imaginary mountains and a quiet humming tune finds its ending.

lectures.title: Todd and the Almost Ocean
lectures.description: Todd and Sue give a small rain puddle an enormous name on a grown-up-accompanied walk to Round Pond.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Dandelion Hat Show
lectures.description: Wendy shows Sue Far Meadow, and a single dandelion becomes the silent audience for a show of hats made from fallen leaves.

lectures.title: The Round Window on the Yellow Map
lectures.description: All six friends meet at Story House, and Sue chooses how her newly familiar cottage will appear on Amy's yellow map before returning home with Grandpa Ed.

lectures.title: The Door That Lost Its Squeak
lectures.description: Amy, Sue and Ben discover that the Story House door no longer squeaks after Grandpa Ed fixes its stiff hinge; Amy keeps the old sound mark on her map.

lectures.title: Ben and the Very Small Welcome Committee
lectures.description: Ben tries to replace the missing squeak with a committee made of a pebble and a leaf; a wiggly wave works better, and the committee retires.

lectures.title: Sue and the Castle Bakery Door
lectures.description: At Round Window Cottage, Sue adds a small flap door to her cardboard castle bakery and invents window orders for customers who cannot fit through it.

lectures.title: Kim and the Little Click
lectures.description: Kim visits the newly quiet Story House with Todd, whose damp yellow boots say shup; she notices the small click of the repaired door latch.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Knock-Knock Hat
lectures.description: Wind makes Wendy's blue hat ribbon tap the Story House doorframe, and Ben thinks the quiet door has learned to knock.

lectures.title: The House with the Quiet Door
lectures.description: All six friends enjoy an ordinary Story House afternoon; Amy keeps the old squeak curl on her map and adds a small blue dot for the new latch click.

lectures.title: The Green Bus Past the Meadow
lectures.description: Amy and Wendy discover the green bus stop west of Far Meadow and ride with Grandma May and Aunt Kay to the next town’s Market Street.

lectures.title: Ben and the Pigeon Parade
lectures.description: Ben takes the green bus with Amy and discovers that Market Street’s pigeons have no interest in marching in his parade.

lectures.title: Kim and the Library Window
lectures.description: Kim and Sue explore the public library on Market Street and Kim borrows a picture book featuring a wheeled blue sock.

lectures.title: Todd and the Bread with a Hole
lectures.description: Todd and Ben look through ring-shaped bread at the bakery on Market Street and consider the practical problems of bread-shaped boots.

lectures.title: Sue and the Clock with No Pockets
lectures.description: Sue wonders where Market Street’s shop clock stores its minutes, then draws a clock with pockets for her cardboard castle bakery.

lectures.title: Another Fold for Amy’s Map
lectures.description: Six friends revisit Market Street; Kim returns her library book, and Amy extends her yellow map with a fold-out panel for the bus journey.

lectures.title: The Garden That Grew Past Its Sign
lectures.description: Amy and Ben find the once-small garden tall with sunflower stalks; Grandma May explains the radish harvest, and Amy adds an in-between sketch to the existing folder.

lectures.title: Ben and the Sign That Went Missing
lectures.description: Ben and Sue search for the garden sign hidden by a sunflower leaf until Grandpa Ed and Grandma May move it to a readable place along the dry path.

lectures.title: Kim and the Empty Row
lectures.description: Kim visits the now-empty radish row and sees a beetle and moving leaf shadows, while keeping the three special stones in her pouch.

lectures.title: Todd and the Bud with Its Coat On
lectures.description: Todd compares his old first-sprout drawing with the tall sunflower buds; on a later visit he sees the first narrow line of yellow.

lectures.title: Wendy and the Flower Without a Hat
lectures.description: Wendy finds the first sunflower open, jokes with Ben about its size and leaves the flower to itself, taking her little paper hat home.

lectures.title: Two Pictures of the Same Garden
lectures.description: The six friends draw the now-tall garden beside the original seedling picture; Amy adds a yellow flower dot to her real map.

lectures.title: The Note in the Library Window
lectures.description: Kim and Sue find a note inviting homemade books to the Market Street library and remember Ben's completed Book of Little Sounds.

lectures.title: Ben and the Book's Traveling Coat
lectures.description: Ben decides to take his six-page blue sound book to the library, checks its exact pages, and chooses a plain cloth bag for the journey.

lectures.title: Todd and the Audience of One Chair
lectures.description: Todd practices reading his bup page to a chair, while Kim chooses how she would like to participate without public speaking.

lectures.title: The Bus with a Book in Its Belly
lectures.description: The six friends take Ben's cloth-wrapped book on the green bus to Market Street, where the librarian keeps it safe overnight for Sunday.

lectures.title: Kim and the Table by the Window
lectures.description: The friends show their six sound pages at the Market Street library; Kim chooses a small way to contribute, and Ben receives a thank-you bookmark.

lectures.title: The Book That Came Home
lectures.description: Ben returns his six-page Book of Little Sounds to the Story House shelf, with a paper thank-you bookmark remembering its Market Street visit.

seasons.title: The Green Bus to Market Street
The Book That Took the Bus
